html:
The scene in 1596 when the first Dutch fleet to reach Asia, under Cornelis de Houtman, anchored off Bantam in west Java, and traders from across Asia came aboard to buy and sell, turning the decks into a market.

Dutch accounts describe Javanese, Chinese, Gujarati, Bengali, Arab, Persian and Malay merchants offering pepper, spices, cloth and food. The visit went badly: de Houtman quarrelled with the Banten court and left with little pepper, but the voyage showed the way, and the Dutch East India Company followed in 1602.

The scene sits at the centre of an old argument. The Dutch historian J. C. van Leur said Asian trade was mostly a peddling trade, many small merchants carrying small loads. Later historians answered that great merchants with large capital, ships and agents also worked these markets. See also pepper.
